findings.title: Salesforce: `prisma` is used but never imported
findings.body: The new code calls `prisma.credential.update(...)`, but this file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`. It fails type-check, and at runtime throws a ReferenceError on every Salesforce client construction.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh bypasses credential sync and runs on every construction
findings.body: The new token refresh is a direct fetch to login.salesforce.com. It does not use `refreshOAuthTokens`, so it never calls the sync endpoint. It also runs unconditionally in every service constructor, not only when the token has expired. This adds a network call and a DB write per instantiation. The resulting connection still uses the old `credentialKey.access_token` instead of the freshly fetched one, so the refresh has no effect on the connection it builds. The refresh also needs the actual refresh_token, but with credential sync enabled the fallback `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` placeholder would be stored.

findings.title: Broken computed-key zod schema
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to a literal string such as "[object Object]" or "ZodString", not a catch-all key. The schema therefore requires a property with that literal name, and `safeParse` fails for any real token response. When sync is enabled, every refresh throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". The intended pattern is `.passthrough()` or `.catchall()`.

findings.title: Dummy refresh_token written into the data, and the non-sync path is changed
findings.body: A missing refresh_token is replaced with the string "refresh_token", and this runs even when credential sync is disabled. For schemas without `refresh_token` this also mutates the parsed data, adding a bogus field. The placeholder could later be stored and used as a real token. In Google's CalendarService the result of this function (a SafeParse object `{success, data}`) is saved as `key`, so the DB credential becomes `{success:true,data:{...}}` and loses its token fields.

findings.title: Credential key stored as a safeParse result object
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod safeParse result, not the parsed data. Storing it as `key` corrupts the credential, since Google would later fail to read access_token or refresh_token. Previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse` returned the data directly. Also, with sync enabled, `res?.data` is undefined for a fetch `Response`, which makes `token.access_token` throw.

findings.title: Sync endpoint response has different shape than callers expect, and no auth or error check
findings.body: The function returns a raw fetch `Response` in the sync case, but the non-sync paths return different shapes. Examples: Google `fetchTokens.res` with `.data`, hubspot a token object, zohocrm/bigin an axios response with `.data`. Hubspot, Google, Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin read `.expiresIn`, `.data` or similar directly off the result, so with sync enabled those properties are undefined and these paths break. There is also no `response.ok` check and no authentication header on the POST to the sync endpoint.

findings.title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time `!==`; unvalidated body and decrypt
findings.body: The secret is compared with a plain `!==`, which is timing-attackable. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual`. `schema.parse` throws on a bad body, which becomes a 500 instead of a 400. `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` can also throw on bad ciphertext and is not caught. There is no method check, so any HTTP method is accepted.

findings.title: Credential lookup/update can collide with teams and existing credentials; keys not validated
findings.body: `findFirst` on userId + appId may match a different credential than intended when a user has several for the app, and a race can create duplicates because there is no unique constraint. Decrypted keys are written to the DB without schema validation per app.

findings.title: Zoho refresh passes userId but synced response will not have `.data` shape
findings.body: With sync enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a fetch Response. The code then reads `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`, which is undefined, so a TypeError is thrown and swallowed by the catch. The token is then never refreshed.

findings.title: Bigin passes credentialId instead of userId
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` expects the Cal.com user id, but `credentialId` is passed here. With sync enabled this sends the wrong id (a credential id) as `calcomUserId`, so the self-hoster's endpoint returns credentials for the wrong user or none. The response shape also differs, as noted for other services.

findings.title: Unrelated change: hardcoded slug in redirect URI
findings.body: The redirect URI was changed from `appConfig.slug` to a hardcoded `zoho-bigin`. The callback still uses `appConfig.slug`, so the two are now inconsistent. This is unrelated to the PR and brittle.
